newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 27.

text.p: Pharmaceuticals company Green Cross Corp is expected to see zero current profit and 500 million yen operating loss in the half-year ending September 30, 1996, because the company was hurt by medical institutions' boycott of its products.
Mazda Motor Corp plans to introduce a new promotion system from 1998 as part of its restructuring plan under the direction of Ford Motor Co.

Matsushita Electronics Corp has purchased a stake of about 10 percent in Symetrix Corp of the United States, a research and development company, to develop materials for ferroelectric flash memory chips.
Mitsubishi Chemical Corp plans to enter the data storage equipment business by selling a magneto-optical (MO) disc jukebox.

Healthy assets at Japan's seven failed housing loans companies have decreased by more than 200 billion yen, as borrowers repaid their loans earlier than expected and switched to lower-rate loans from city banks.

Electric Power Development Co Ltd (EPDC) plans to purchase a 10 percent stake from Idemitsu Kosan in a coal mine in Australia for between one and two billion yen. EPDC needs to obtain a steady source of power for the coal-thermal power plants it is building in Japan.

Fujitsu Ltd's consolidated net profit is expected to fall to 50 and 55 billion yen in the business year to March 1997, down between 13 and 21 percent from a year earlier. This is because Fujitsu's affiliate company Amdahl Corp has posted a net loss of about $288 million in the half year ended June 30, 1996.
